name: Agra
summary: Imperial Mughal capital on the Yamuna river, internationally famous for the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and marble inlay.

profile.Food: Agra Petha, Bedai Aloo, Mughlai curries
profile.Crafts: Pietra dura marble inlay, Leather footwear

points: Home to three UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri
Capital of the Mughal Empire under emperors Akbar, Jahangir, and Shah Jahan

name: Ayodhya
summary: Ancient sacred city on the holy Saryu river, legendary capital of the Ikshvaku dynasty and birthplace of Lord Rama.
points: Birthplace of Lord Rama described in the epic Ramayana; capital of ancient Kosala Kingdom
Home to the newly consecrated grand Ram Mandir and historic Hanuman Garhi temple

name: Lucknow
summary: The City of Nawabs and capital of Uttar Pradesh, famed for refined Tehzeeb manners, Awadhi cuisine, and Chikankari embroidery.

profile.Food: Awadhi Dum Biryani, Galouti Kebab, Sheermal
profile.Crafts: GI-tagged Chikankari white embroidery, Zardozi gold embroidery

points: Capital of the Nawabs of Awadh who built the Bara Imambara and Rumi Darwaza in the 18th century
Bara Imambara features the world's largest unsupported vaulted hall (Bhulbhulaiya maze)

name: Mathura
summary: Sacred Braj Bhumi on the Yamuna river, revered birthplace of Lord Krishna, and ancient seat of Mathura Kushan art.

profile.Crafts: Sanjhi paper stenciling art, Deity dresses

points: Birthplace of Lord Krishna at Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi complex
Major cultural capital of Kushan Empire (1st–3rd century CE) where early red sandstone Buddha and Hindu sculptures evolved

name: Varanasi (Kashi)
summary: Spiritual Capital of India, sacred holy city on the Ganges with 84 bathing ghats and Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga.

profile.Food: Banarasi Paan, Malaiyo, Tamatar Chaat, Kachori Jalebi
profile.Crafts: GI-tagged Banarasi silk brocade sarees, Pink Meenakari enamel, Wooden toys

points: One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited sacred cities, dating back to 2nd millennium BCE
Includes Sarnath, where Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon (Dharmachakra Pravartana) in 528 BCE
